_comment: Categories that will ship BELOW the 5-creator target because the search is finished and this is what exists. Only add an entry once you have actually stopped looking for that specific category — a domain having had one pass proves nothing. Each reason says what was searched and what was found, to the same standard as critic-gaps.json. The 5-minimum is a target the owner knowingly traded away rather than loosen the scope rule; this file is where that trade is made visible. Empty is correct until a category's search is genuinely done.

addiction-recovery.reason: Searched deliberately rather than opportunistically: 13 candidate handles probed, 5 resolved. Included: Addiction Policy Forum (non-profit, interviews named researchers, nothing sold) and Sober Powered (a coach, explicitly not a clinician, whose post-acute withdrawal material is hard to find elsewhere). @NIDAnews is an unrelated Arabic-language news channel; @AlcoholMastery has one upload.
addiction-recovery.challenged: The owner challenged the original exclusion of @TheRecoveryVillage, correctly: it was excluded on conflict of interest alone, which is a stricter standard than this project applies anywhere else — commercial interest is normally disclosed with sells-course or sponsor-heavy and left to the visitor to weigh. Re-examined on content instead. Its long-form output is patient testimonials and staff Q&As, its mid-length band is more testimonials plus admissions and insurance explainers ('Understanding Your Admission Process', '7 Myths Around Using Insurance for Rehab'), and the remainder is generic meditation and nutrition filler unrelated to addiction. It does carry genuinely useful withdrawal-timeline and detox-danger explainers, but those are ~3-minute clips. The deciding test: would this be included if a non-profit ran it? No — the substantive content is too thin and too marketing-shaped, the same standard that excluded GitKraken, Zapier and Big Interview. @AllenCarrsEasyway fails identically: 4 long-form videos, all testimonials. So the exclusions stand, but on content quality rather than on conflict, and the original reasoning was wrong. The commercial-conflict signal was added as a result, so that future cases are disclosed rather than silently dropped.
addiction-recovery.attribution: MIXED, and mostly our criteria rather than absent supply. Supply exists — this is a large, active field on YouTube — but almost all of it is either treatment-provider marketing or unstructured personal testimony. What is genuinely scarce is independent, credentialed, educational content. Under a looser content standard the count would still be 2, because the rejected candidates fail on substance rather than on the rule-12 conflict test; under a looser CREDENTIAL standard it could be higher, since there are many recovery-testimony channels deliberately not pursued.

_schema: Each entry: reason (what was searched and found), gapCause (absent-supply | our-criteria | mixed), countUnderLooserStandard (how many creators the category would hold if our own criteria were relaxed to the standard used elsewhere in the dataset — so a gap caused by our rules is never mistaken for a gap in the world), and challenged (any reasoning that was contested and re-examined).
